svg.title: The Binance book before a top-taker fire, a look-alike our model scores the same, and an ordinary moment
svg.desc: Three columns of three panels: best-level sizes, aggressive trades and the Binance mid change, from -1000 to +300 ms around each moment.
svg.text: What the top taker reacts to, next to a moment our model cannot tell apart from it
Binance futures best level from 1 s before to 0.3 s after each moment (t = 0: for the fire, its order reaching Predict). All three are bets on up: the far side is the ask.
Far side (must empty for the price to move their way); trades hitting it
Typical fire: the top taker's order
far 1.33 · near 11.11 BTC · moved their way +6 ms
Best-level size, BTC (log scale; under 0.1 drawn at 0.1)
Look-alike: same score, no fire, no move
far 1.94 · near 4.90 BTC · no move in 300 ms
far 6.25 · near 5.89 BTC · no move in 300 ms
Across all 4,425 of its fires on these days, Binance moved their way within 300 ms after 61%; after the 22,125 look-alikes our public score rates the same, 7.8%.
A model can tell its fires from the look-alikes (held-out AUC 0.75): more imbalance building, more of the far side withdrawn, as in the left column.
But that look does not predict moves at ordinary moments (AUC 0.50): what tells it when to fire is not in the data we record.
Four consumed days; development evidence. Examples: the fire nearest the median fire on nine key book inputs, and its nearest look-alike.
